metadata.description: Android installer app that runs the real RuneLite client on Samsung Tab S10 Ultra via Termux + proot-distro
metadata.session_notes: Session 77: Diagnosed proot ptrace syscall interception as the confirmed FPS bottleneck. Built /proc off-CPU sampler (scripts/jvm-wait-sampler.sh + jvm-wait-analyze.py) and captured 60s at Varrock East Bank: Client thread shows 3945 nonvol ctxt-switches/s, math works out to exactly 12 FPS ceiling (1970 syscalls/s ÷ 164 per frame). A/B'd RLT_PROOT_SECCOMP=1 — seccomp-bpf engages but Samsung OneUI kernel doesn't route SECCOMP_RET_TRACE; execve ENOSYS → launch fails. Proot 5.1.107-70 latest in Termux main, no upgrade path. User widened scope (Termux + RLT app forkable; RL + Android off-limits). Chose Option B: native-Termux JVM, skip proot-distro Ubuntu entirely. Installed openjdk-21, mesa, X11 libs, patchelf via Termux apt. rlawt-1.8.jar's bundled linux-aarch64/librlawt.so is glibc-linked with full VERNEED/VERSYM metadata. 4 YOLO workarounds (symlink → bionic paths, symlink → permitted namespace paths, patchelf --remove-needed/--replace-needed, gobjcopy --remove-section=.gnu.version_r) all failed at successive Bionic-linker glibc-rejection layers. Clean fix is rebuilding rlawt via Android NDK (Task 21, 2-4h). Three new analysis docs under runelite-tablet/docs/logs/. New memory: project_ptrace_is_the_fps_bottleneck.md.

current_phase.phase_name: 120 FPS Presentation — S77 diagnosed proot ptrace bottleneck; Option B (native-Termux JVM) chosen, blocked on rlawt Bionic rebuild

active_blockers.description: rlawt-1.8.jar ships net/runelite/rlawt/linux-aarch64/librlawt.so as a glibc-linked ELF (NEEDED libc.so.6 + ld-linux-aarch64.so.1, full VERNEED/VERSYM sections). Termux's JVM is Bionic. Bionic's linker rejects glibc libs at 4 layers (NEEDED / namespace / VERNEED / VERSYM / vn_version). 4 YOLO workarounds in S77 hit successive rejections — the clean path is rebuild via Android NDK. rlawt's symbol surface is small and Bionic-ABI-compatible (no pthread, no exotic glibc); only metadata blocks. Task 21.

Upstream of rlawt blocker. S77 /proc-sampler measurement: RuneLite Client thread 3945 nonvoluntary ctxt-switches/s under default proot ptrace mode = synchronous syscall interception = ~2000 syscalls/s throughput ceiling = 12 FPS at 164 syscalls/frame (GL plugin). Cheap fix (RLT_PROOT_SECCOMP=1 seccomp-bpf) fails on Samsung OneUI kernel: kernel doesn't deliver SECCOMP_RET_TRACE events to proot, execve gets ENOSYS, proot-distro login dies. Proot 5.1.107-70 is latest in Termux main. Unblocks when Option B (native-Termux JVM, removes proot from hot path) is wired — which depends on the rlawt blocker above. Fallback: Task 20 (fork + patch proot seccomp filter).

resolved_blockers.description: S74 theorized Samsung OneUI's /background cpuset (CPUs 0-3) was clamping Termux subtree and thus FPS. S75-S76 landed Path A (bindService hoist to /top-app) with perfect scheduler landing (JVM+virgl on cpus 4-7). S76 measured FPS at 12-15 (vs 13 baseline). Scene FPS did not move. S77 /proc sampler showed system is 70%+ idle — pipeline is not CPU-bound. Cpuset was never the gate.
resolved_blockers.resolution: Session 76: Path A measured null. Session 77: /proc sampler confirmed sink is proot ptrace (3945 nonvol/s on Client), not CPU contention.

resolved_blockers.description: Originally 'per-PutImage-strip overhead'. Reframed in S74: compositor has 2.5x idle headroom, real bottleneck is upstream. Reframed again in S77: the real sink is proot ptrace interception of JVM syscalls.
resolved_blockers.resolution: Session 77: Bottleneck definitively identified as proot ptrace syscall interception. Tracked now as proot-ptrace-syscall-interception-caps-fps-at-12.

resolved_blockers.description: DamageTraceV2 proved the hot steady-state path is PutImage on WINDOW with backend=other, not fbPutImage or miPutImage.
resolved_blockers.resolution: Session 72: extended DamageTraceV2 with dladdr offset logging and routed through __android_log_print. addr2line resolved the unknown backend to `exaPutImage` @ xserver/exa/exa_accel.c:252, and exaComposite @ xserver/exa/exa_render.c:887. Both sit inside the EXA acceleration framework. Follow-on Slice 3 fix (lorieUploadToScreen) made the path 99.6% accelerated.

resolved_blockers.description: Session 70 concluded VirGL vtest socket serialization was the structural FPS ceiling (17-28ms inter-frame).
resolved_blockers.resolution: Session 72 REFUTED this. VirGL throughput was never the bottleneck. S77 also confirmed — virgl main thread vol_rate 270/s matches current FPS × msg/frame, not elevated.
